heading: INT. BRIDAL SHOP - FITTING ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. BRIDAL SHOP - FITTING ROOM - DAY
A velvet-curtained cubicle, mirrors on three walls.
A wedding gown on a hanger.
ADELAIDE VOSSBERG, twenties, in a slip, stands on the dais, arms out.
Her mother GERTRUDE, fifties, kneels with a mouthful of pins.
Stand still.
units.name: GERTRUDE

units.text: I am standing still.
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: A WOMAN in a sensible coat peers through the curtain.
Sixties, hair in a bun, hands wringing.
Neither of them has seen her before.
Pardon me. Is this the Vossberg fitting?
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: It is. And you are?
units.name: GERTRUDE

units.text: Just someone who used to know the groom's father.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: Gertrude's pins clatter to the floor.
Adelaide turns on the dais.
Mother?
units.name: ADELAIDE

units.text: You'd better come in.
units.name: GERTRUDE

units.text: The Woman steps inside, letting the curtain fall.
She holds out a gloved hand.
Tillie. Tillie Marchetti.
units.name: WOMAN

units.text: I know who you are.
units.name: GERTRUDE

units.text: Then you know why I'm here.
units.name: TILLIE

units.text: He asked me to give you something, dear.
units.name: TILLIE

units.text: Adelaide looks from one to the other in the three mirrors, six faces, six mothers.
Will someone please tell me what's going on?
units.name: ADELAIDE
